# Rebase plan

Ours is the new base; theirs is the issue-374 commit being replayed. Combine the base's review-history feature with the approved bounded direct-issue continuation work. History is advisory evidence, not approval, rejection provenance, pair-completion evidence, or retry allowance. This document proposes resolutions only; no conflicted source files are resolved.

## docs/WORKFLOWS.md
Ours: Expands rejected-plan documentation with authenticated direct-issue review rounds, retry-versus-round accounting, prior findings delivered to reviewers, revision-scoped history, status guidance, actionable rejection notes, and planner steering after a reset. Retains the older single-review invocation and invocation-local validation-repair descriptions.
Theirs: Documents default direct-issue continuation to trusted validation, persisted replan and repair allowances, durable human approval obligations, role-specific feedback and --next admission, explicit phase/handoff boundaries, state-dependent WorkUnit-edit recovery, restricted manual staging, requested developer rounds, and separate submit. Preserves separate PR/node behavior.
Resolution: Use the continuation and recovery descriptions from theirs, incorporating ours' review-history, review-round and status explanations. State clearly that review rounds and retry reservations differ, and earlier findings cannot approve current content. Scope the single-review promise to opted-out PR/node paths. Keep manual staging conditional on plan mode and authorization; distinguish agent retry accounting from the separate human-draft obligation and allowance. Do not retain a generic reset-then-plan recipe that promises a draft at zero or with missing reports. Preserve actionable --notes and planner steering examples only where the documented state permits them.
Approved behavior: Preserves PLAN.md's R2 feedback matrix, R5 existing recovery routes, persistent bounds, fresh exact-pair human approval under every direct-issue gate, explicit boundaries, and no automatic publishing, while retaining the base's useful reviewer continuity documentation.

## internal/lease/manager.go
Ours: Adds PlanReviewHistory and PlanReviewSequence to IssueState, clears history when approved task/base/policy identity changes, and appends authenticated human review history in both review replacement and insertion branches.
Theirs: Adds human rejection/draft, generation/reservation/completion, and persistent validation-repair state; strengthens legacy rejection hydration; preserves or clears obligations according to task changes; checks pair completeness and human obligations at review, implementation, validation and approval admission; invalidates completion on single writes; routes human decisions through recordPlanReviewTransition; adds fenced trusted-base validation repair reservation.
Resolution: Retain both sets of IssueState fields and both invalidation policies: revision-scoped history may clear on task/base/policy changes, but identical-task human rejection identity and spent draft allowance survive base/policy and branch movement. Changed WorkUnit clears obsolete obligation and generation tracking; approved identity changes reset validation repair only as specified. In each successful RecordHumanReview insertion/replacement branch call recordPlanReviewTransition once, with that helper appending history once; do not also append history at the call site. Preserve missing-report refusal for both human verdicts, incomplete-pair approval refusal, direct-issue-only safety gates before GateNone, trusted provenance checks, and fenced reservation behavior. Keep history clearing independent from approval/carry evidence and preserve PR/fork exclusions.
Approved behavior: Maintains authoritative typed state, exact-content human approval, claim fencing, durable counters across claims, R1 pair safety and R3/N4 obligation persistence. Review history remains informational and cannot weaken any admission or reset the human draft budget.

## internal/lease/plan_replan.go
Ours: Adds bounded authenticated review history (eight entries, UTF-8-safe 16 KiB findings), revision-filtered history projection, independent review-round calculation, direct-review scoping, and CurrentPlanRejection requiring the current bound authenticated rejection. Appends history from recordPlanReviewTransition.
Theirs: Extends PlanRejection with source, findings and rejected report digests; records durable human obligations; reserves fenced agent/human attempts; adds complete pair generations and reservation identity, atomic RecordPlanPair, meaningful-change checks, revised-pair detection, and state-dependent exhaustion guidance. Marks authorized staged pairs complete without clearing human obligations.
Resolution: Merge the history helpers/imports with the durable rejection, pair and reservation implementation. Append authenticated non-advisory history once at the start of the shared review transition, retaining the human-obligation transition and existing PR/fork behavior. Keep CurrentPlanRejection's narrow meaning for status of a current bound rejection; do not substitute it for retained rejection feedback, human obligation, or HasRevisedPlan when reports were replaced or bindings moved. Keep history bounded and revision-scoped independently of retained human findings. Resolve pair admission according to PLAN.md's exact DirectIssue AND (rejection/obligation OR tracked generation) AND NOT complete-generation predicate; absent reports must still fail review/approval while an authorized, budgeted regeneration remains possible. Do not let the replay's absent-report shortcut erase tracked/rejection safety state. Preserve marker-less initial compatibility, one-report-body revisions in a committed pair, CAS atomicity, reservation matching and mode-aware recovery guidance.
Approved behavior: Preserves R1 complete-generation provenance separately from approval bindings, R2 bounded feedback-driven planning, and R5 missing-report recovery without report-less human review or promises of a draft at zero. Base history cannot mint approval or replenish allowances; moved-binding retained findings remain usable solely as planner guidance.

## internal/lease/plan_replan_test.go
Ours: Adds history assertions to existing advisory and task-reapproval tests and tests history authentication, bounding/truncation, human decisions, task/policy/base invalidation, untrusted/stale/unauthorized writes, and rebase persistence. Its history loop revises one report with UpdateArtifact before submitting another review.
Theirs: Converts rejected-plan and staging fixtures to RecordPlanPair and adds pair-predicate, atomicity, unchanged-report/version tampering, human obligation across gates, persisted repair budget/fencing, and changed-versus-identical WorkUnit branch-invalidation regressions, including missing-report human-review refusal.
Resolution: Retain both test families and required imports. Use complete atomic pairs in ordinary direct-issue fixtures. Adapt the history loop to reserve the appropriate replan attempt and record a complete revised pair before reviewing; arrange a sufficient trusted fixture allowance for its history-length exercise rather than bypassing admission or resetting production counters. Preserve deliberate single-write cases as incomplete-pair rejection tests. Keep all history, authentication, UTF-8, stale-binding and advisory assertions alongside pair/draft/repair assertions. Align absent-report predicate coverage with PLAN.md's R1 invariant and separately prove authorized regeneration, missing-report review refusal, retained findings, and unchanged human consumption. Human review history must increment once even when that same decision establishes an obligation.
Approved behavior: Tests both features without weakening mixed-pair protection, exact human approval, claim fences or persisted budgets. Covers R1/R3/N4/N5 and preserves existing adversarial tests rather than treating history fixtures as exceptions to authorization.

## internal/workflow/engine_test.go
Ours: Adds a workflow test for rejected-plan feedback continuity, planner reservation telemetry, review-history evidence and prompts, fresh report bindings and stale-approval refusal. Adds role/revision scope tests excluding planner/developer/tester and PR/fork/gateway bundles from history. The lifecycle test intentionally uses separate opted-out invocations.
Theirs: Adds TestIssueWorkOutputExpiredRecoveryClaim, proving recovery guidance asks for release only while a claim is active and unexpired, otherwise proceeding to the maintainer edit route.
Resolution: Retain both additions and the workspace import. Preserve the history lifecycle's opted-out first-invocation rejection stop and explicit plan/review boundaries; retain its reservation-count and exact-current-binding assertions under atomic pair recording. Keep history role/protocol scoping tests intact and retain both active and expired claim recovery cases. Do not enable IssueContinuation globally in old lifecycle fixtures merely to make the merge pass; default continuation remains covered by the separate opted-in and real CLI tests required by the approved plan.
Approved behavior: Preserves R4 opted-out engine behavior, independent review and evidence scoping, planner telemetry reflecting durable reservations, and R5 actionable state-dependent recovery without unnecessary release instructions for expired claims.

## internal/workflow/execute_plan.go
Ours: Refreshes r.st and r.res.State from the successful fenced UpdatePhase before compiling the planner bundle, exposing the actual reserved retry count to prompts and telemetry; also populates result state for interactive planning.
Theirs: Adds bare-rejection feedback admission, moves progress reporting after reservation, reports human/agent retry usage, refreshes r.st from UpdatePhase, records direct-issue reports atomically with RecordPlanPair, retains separate PR/fork writes, and wraps unchanged-pair failure as rejected-plan termination.
Resolution: Keep theirs' admission, retry progress, atomic pair recording and unchanged-output handling, and preserve ours' result-state refresh: assign the UpdatePhase return to r.st, then r.res.State before bundle compilation and planner invocation. Keep interactive result-state initialization and boundary behavior. Emit retry counts from the refreshed authoritative state after reservation; do not reserve again for telemetry or bundle setup. Preserve effective planner instruction delivery, retained rejection feedback, and PR/fork separate-write behavior. A human replacement draft still stops for fresh authenticated approval; history and agent verdicts cannot authorize continuation through that obligation.
Approved behavior: Supports bounded same-invocation replanning with accurate persisted budget output, preserves failure spending and prompt/role selections, prevents mixed report pairs, and retains explicit phase/handoff and human approval boundaries required by PLAN.md.

artifacts.body:
# ISSUE-374 implementation plan

Default direct issue work will continue through authorized planning, review, implementation, testing and trusted validation to a checkpoint. It will use typed authoritative state, preserve operator choices and stop when a decision or unsafe condition blocks progress. Publishing remains a separate explicit action.

## Dimensions and feasibility

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive. Apply the approved sensitive profile, with independent adversarial review of admission, persistence and approval. Estimate 10–14 hours for implementation and validation within the 16-hour total claim budget; reopen for decomposition if the persistence changes cannot fit that budget.

## Review disposition

Earlier feedback “cleaning up and re-running” adds no requirement. Preserve resolved F1–F4 findings as described here; the authenticated review supplied with this request is the evidence for R1–R4, with the current `.swarm/active/REVIEW.md` checked against source. R1 is resolved by the exact predicate and checkpoint writer rules below; R2 by the operator-feedback matrix and matching tests. R3 separates generation completion from approval binding and preserves human obligations through carry removal; R4 requires real CLI-path continuation regressions and preserves opted-out engine assertions. N3 retains the all-pre-existing refusal without developer instructions, including explicit implement. This plan replaces the previous attempt: durable pair provenance addresses F1, fenced human-draft accounting addresses F2, a state-scoped human obligation addresses F3, and pre-claim selection classification addresses F4.

R5 uses the reviewer-permitted existing-route option: keep report-less human review refused, and name a maintainer WorkUnit edit and separate reapproval when agent planning cannot produce another draft. N4 covers branch-change invalidation; N5 separates retained feedback delivery from approval binding validity. Resolved R1–R4 and F1–F4 remain intact.

## What we know

- `internal/workflow/engine.go:511` ExecuteWork coordinates the lifecycle; `engine.go:900` stops on rejected review. `execute_plan.go:24,65,96` already supplies rejection feedback and rejects a replan only when both canonical reports are unchanged.
- `execute_plan.go:103,107` writes the two reports separately. `internal/lease/manager.go:1898` deletes review artifacts on either report replacement. `internal/lease/plan_replan.go:15` retains rejection identity but no rejected report digests or pair completion evidence. Comparing two changed digests cannot prove a complete pair, and one unchanged report is a legitimate revision.
- `plan_replan.go:25,86` resets pending rejection for human review and reserves agent replan attempts in fenced phase mutation. `manager.go:1509,1564` authenticates human review but clears that pending state. Human drafts therefore need separate durable accounting.
- `manager.go:1557` refuses both human verdicts if either report is missing; `plan_replan.go:117` disables manual staging in agent mode. `internal/cli/issue_edit.go:43,115,236` supports structured edits, checks digest changes and rejects active claims; `internal/cli/issue.go:112` registers separate task approval. Preserve those authority boundaries.
- `manager.go:786` handles changed task/base/policy together. `VerifyApproval` around `manager.go:2426` admits GateNone before reviewing artifacts. A human rejection obligation must survive base-only changes and be enforced before that early return.
- `execute_validation.go:124` bounds repair per invocation today. `execute_implementation.go:255` verifies tester retry eligibility; `execute_validation.go:45,105,111` selects retry checks and the fenced RecordRetryValidation write using explicit test phase. Default tester resume needs the same checks.
- `internal/cli/work.go:79,106` shares numbered/--next options but overwrites requested phase with selection's derived entry phase. `selection.go:127,133` derives handoff phase and filters only some blocked states. `engine.go:415,481` and `execute_setup.go:120` independently choose/preflight roles.
- `docs/WORKFLOWS.md:233,241` promises one review round and invocation-local repair. `docs/developer.md:354,361` promises a fresh repair budget. Makefile's check target runs lint, race tests and changelog-check.

## What we're assuming

Existing IssueState serialization can carry optional coordinator-owned fields without fork protocol changes. Confirm state copies, resets and gateway admission before implementation. Missing fields never prove completed rejection-replacement provenance; marker-less pairs without rejection remain compatible as specified below. No paid harness or live GitHub is needed for deterministic acceptance tests.

## Open questions

Git metadata is unavailable here (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails). `changes/unreleased/374.md` is absent in the snapshot, but approved-base absence cannot be confirmed. Before writing that path, the developer must inspect `git cat-file -e '<base_sha>:changes/unreleased/374.md'`; describe it as modified if present and added only if absent. All other planned source/test/doc paths already exist; no new source/test file is proposed. Live GitHub/harness checks belong in PR review and do not block sandbox implementation.

Pre-upgrade state can have lost a human rejection artifact after report replacement. Its history cannot be reconstructed from current artifacts. Stop with state-dependent R5 recovery guidance when legacy rejection/pair evidence is incomplete; do not claim to recognize deleted human reviews. If all rejection evidence was already erased before upgrade, current state cannot retrospectively establish the obligation; document this migration limitation for maintainer review.

## Transition matrix

Continuation applies only to direct local/GitHub issue work with operator-requested all, including --next. Add an explicit IssueContinuation opt-in and preserve RequestedPhase separately from selection-derived entry phase. Node, PR and fork do not acquire continuation. A durable human obligation is a narrow state-safety exception enforced for every direct-issue caller, including node, explicit phases, stage and submit.

| Authoritative condition | Action | Stop condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No usable plan | Planner produces and records a complete pair | Interactive plan, split recommendation, refusal or invalid output |
| Actionable bound agent rejection | Reserve existing replan allowance, pass durable feedback, revise, review again | Exhaustion or canonical unchanged pair |
| Actionable human rejection | Reserve its durable draft allowance, produce at most one revised draft per invocation | Always stop for fresh authenticated human approval; failure/unchanged output does not refund allowance |
| Completed revised pair with pending rejection | Verify durable pair completion and rejected provenance, review without planner or reservation | Invalid rejected provenance; approval bindings are checked separately, not as pair incompleteness |
| Marker-less existing pair, no rejection or human obligation, no tracked generation | Preserve existing review/approval eligibility and exact bindings; no migration reservation | Missing/invalid reports follow existing rules; absence of a new marker alone never strands pre-upgrade work |
| Interrupted pair or incomplete legacy provenance under the predicate below | Stop; never review/approve mixed reports | Human decision using the state-dependent R5 routes below; never suggest report-less review or promise a draft at zero |
| Bare/empty rejection findings | Apply operator-feedback matrix below | Without planner feedback stop without reservation |
| Human obligation or configured human gate | Await exact authenticated human approval | Agent APPROVED and GateNone cannot bypass it |
| Complete pair awaiting agent review | Independent sandboxed reviewer | Rejection loops only within allowance; malformed verdict/error stops |
| Exact approval or GateNone without human obligation | Admit authorized next stage | Stale task/plan/policy bindings stop |
| Derived plan/review/implement/test entry under requested all | Continue from eligible authoritative stage | Unknown/unsafe entry stops; derived implement grants no uncounted repair |
| Verified completed implementation, testing incomplete | Tester only, then required checks | Changed head/tree/branch, dirty or ambiguous candidate stops |
| Bound trusted validation already passed | Reuse after checking candidate/task/plan/policy applicability | Invalid evidence cannot report completion |
| Recorded trusted regression/mixed failure | Reserve persisted repair before developer, including resume round zero | Exhaustion or unchanged repair; operator-requested round and pre-existing failures follow matrix below |
| Explicit implement | One requested developer round subject to existing all-pre-existing refusal without developer instructions; automatic repairs use remaining persisted allowance | Never replenish automatic allowance; retain explicit phase/handoff semantics |
| Tester FAIL/BLOCKED or process failure | Preserve failure and eligible retry guidance | No automatic process retry, including refusal/security failure |
| Trusted required checks pass | Return validated checkpoint | Never publish/submit/merge |
| Explicit phase/handoff, claim-budget pause | Preserve requested boundary and current pause semantics | No continuation past boundary |
| Cancellation, fence loss, credentials/isolation/policy/import failure | Stop promptly, preserve wrapped error | No later role or success |

## R1: exact incomplete-pair predicate and writers

Define DirectIssue as non-fork state with no linked PR/revision context; apply the new predicate only there. Let R mean a durable rejection record/pending rejection or human obligation exists (including authenticated legacy review evidence); T mean a coordinator generation has been tracked; C mean both current report versions and digests belong to one committed generation. C proves only pair completion. Existing ApprovalTransition/reviewBaseMatches and verifyReviewBinding checks judge task/base/policy validity; rejection provenance retains its own exact bindings. A base or policy move does not itself invalidate C or require coordinator rebinding. Carried approval can admit unchanged complete reports, while a superseded decision requires fresh approval on those same reports. IncompletePair = DirectIssue AND (R OR T) AND NOT C. Missing/invalid reports and stale approvals still fail their existing checks independently. Thus no R, no T, marker-less initial/pre-upgrade pair is eligible under existing rules; both reports do not need rewriting merely to upgrade. R without C blocks even if both current bodies differ from rejected bodies. T without matching C blocks even with no rejection. Single writes invalidate C but retain T, so they cannot turn tracked state back into legacy compatibility. A valid C permits one unchanged report body. Atomic failure preserves prior artifacts/C. Fork and PR separate writers (`internal/fork/coordinator.go:425`, `internal/cli/stage.go:180,189`) retain existing admission, counters and behavior; do not apply this predicate or require generation metadata there. Existing two-write approval fixtures without R/T remain valid.

All direct-issue pair writers must participate: ordinary planner completion, authorized plan staging, and `RecordCheckpointPlan` (`internal/lease/checkpoint_reconcile.go:563`). The latter keeps its atomic prepared fence and candidate/predecessor metadata and mints the same complete generation inside its successful CAS. `executeCheckpointPlan` (`internal/workflow/execute_plan.go`, reviewer branch :299 and writer call :341) reserves a human draft before launching its planner, using the same rejection identity/limit as normal planning, and refreshes its prepared observation after reservation. Zero/exhausted allowance refuses before planner; failed/unchanged/refused/canceled output spends the admitted attempt. Recording validates the reservation without charging twice. Agent replan reservation retains existing accounting. A human obligation survives checkpoint pair recording and agent APPROVED; checkpoint review may record an advisory agent verdict but cannot authorize reconcile or implementation. Human-gated agent review retains its existing refusal. Reconcile and downstream approval verification require fresh authenticated exact-pair human approval under every gate. No checkpoint/import route can mint human approval or reset draft accounting.

## R2: operator feedback and admission matrix

Use existing `instructionsFor(role)` resolution for general and role-specific text, preserving precedence and prompt delivery. Instructions are guidance within approved scope, never approval. A nonempty effective developer instruction requests one initial developer round per invocation, preserving the existing round-zero override (`execute_implementation.go:64–66`), just as explicit implement requests its first round subject to existing admission. Explicit implement without effective developer instructions still refuses all-pre-existing failures (`execute_implementation.go:64–66`); phase selection does not override that refusal. This round consumes no automatic repair allowance and does not reset it, even at limit zero/exhaustion. It is not automatically repeated; subsequent automatic repairs reserve remaining allowance. Refusal, unchanged output, fencing and security stops still terminate. A failed requested round cannot loop merely because its instruction remains present. This deliberate requested-round distinction preserves the supported override while bounding automatic work.

| Default all condition | General / relevant role feedback | Admission, accounting and stop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bare bound rejection, remaining plan/draft allowance | `--instructions` or `--planner-instructions` supplies effective planner feedback | One planner with feedback plus recorded verdict; reserve existing agent replan or human draft attempt. Agent path can review/continue; human path stops for fresh approval. No invented authenticated findings. |
| Bare bound rejection, no effective planner feedback (including developer/tester/reviewer-only text) | None for planner | Zero planner, no reservation; suggest `swarm issue work N --planner-instructions 'Address …'` with preserved context. Missing rejection provenance still blocks regardless of text. |
| Any rejection, plan/draft limit zero or exhausted | Any text | Zero planner, no budget reset. Select an existing recovery using R5: missing reports in agent mode require a changed WorkUnit and separate reapproval; a fresh rejection is useful only with both reports present and a positive draft limit. At zero, never promise a new draft. |
| All-pre-existing trusted failures, allowance remaining, zero or exhausted | `--instructions` or `--developer-instructions` supplies effective developer feedback | One requested developer round, no counter increment/reset; test and trusted validate. Further automatic repair requires remaining allowance and a repairable regression/mixed failure. |
| All-pre-existing failures | No effective developer feedback, including planner/tester/reviewer-only text | Zero developer, no reservation; suggest `swarm issue work N --developer-instructions 'Address …'`. |
| Regression/mixed trusted failures, remaining allowance | No effective developer feedback | Reserve one automatic repair before developer, including resumed round zero. |
| Regression/mixed trusted failures, zero/exhausted allowance | No effective developer feedback | Zero developer; suggest `swarm issue work N --phase implement` (one requested round, no reset). |
| Regression/mixed trusted failures, remaining/zero/exhausted allowance | Effective developer feedback | Same single requested round as pre-existing override; retain counters, then use only remaining automatic allowance. |
| Any row under `--next` | Same effective role text | Selection classifies with the same options before claim: eligible instructed issue is selected, its feedback delivered, not silently skipped. Blocked issue is skipped with reason/counters; continue scanning without consuming feedback or budgets. Final no-ready output gives the corresponding contextual command/reason. Recheck fenced admission after claim. |

Role-inapplicable feedback never grants a run for a different role. General instructions can reach both planner and developer but confer neither approval nor automatic allowance. Preserve all role/backend/repository overrides through each transition. Document these examples and requested-versus-automatic accounting in docs/developer.md and docs/WORKFLOWS.md.

## R5: state-dependent existing recovery routes (AC3–AC6)

Do not widen `RecordHumanReview`: both APPROVED and CHANGES_REQUESTED remain refused if either report is missing, for direct issues as well as existing PR/fork paths. WorkUnit editing is a maintainer decision, never an automatic continuation step or a way to expand this implementation's scope.

- **Reports absent, human obligation, agent plan mode, zero/exhausted draft allowance:** explain that the identical WorkUnit cannot recover in this state. Name a substantive maintainer edit using `swarm issue edit N --objective '<maintainer-chosen revised objective>'`, followed by separate `swarm issue approve N`, then `swarm issue work N`. The edit must change the canonical WorkUnit digest and remain a deliberate approved contract revision; reapproving identical content, changing only base/policy, restarting or reclaiming cannot help. If an active claim exists, first name `swarm issue release N` for its owner; another actor must follow existing maintainer claim controls. Preserve backend/repository context. Do not suggest review-plan, stage, or discard-checkpoint as recovery in this no-checkpoint state.
- **Reports absent with remaining draft allowance:** retained authenticated findings can guide one reserved replacement draft despite moved base/policy bindings. Their historic bindings never authorize current approval or pair reuse. Stop for fresh exact-pair human approval after replacement.
- **Both reports present, positive trusted limit:** authenticated `swarm issue review-plan N --reject --notes 'Actionable revision request'` may establish a new bounded draft identity, followed by `swarm issue work N --phase plan`; approval still requires a complete pair. A current complete eligible pair may instead receive exact authenticated approval. At limit zero, re-rejection does not grant a planner run. Mixed/incomplete pairs cannot receive approval.
- **Manual staging:** name `swarm issue stage N --phase plan` only outside agent plan mode, in an authorized managed worktree with a valid active claim and both completed reports, satisfying existing staging fences and bindings. It records a complete generation but never clears the human obligation or replenishes the separate human-draft allowance; fresh exact-pair approval is still required. If these prerequisites cannot be met, use the changed-WorkUnit route. Never promise manual staging from agent mode.

Implement this choice in typed stop classification and contextual output (`internal/lease/plan_replan.go:70`, workflow result/progress and CLI next-action paths); do not execute guidance strings. Apply it to missing-report carry stops, limit-zero marker-less/mixed pairs and numbered/--next output. Document why the edit and separate reapproval are needed. Only offer authorized discard when a real eligible checkpoint and its existing expected-head requirements exist.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. **Durable review and pair state (F1–F3).** Modify IssueState and fenced mutation paths in `internal/lease/manager.go`, `plan_replan.go` and existing tests. Extend PlanRejection (or a common coordinator-owned rejection record) with authenticated review identity/version/body digest, actionable findings, source, rejected design/test digests, task/policy/base and draft attempt consumption. Capture these before report replacement deletes the review. Imported metadata cannot supply these fields. Keep human obligation separate from pending agent scheduling so agent approval cannot clear it.

   Add coordinator-only complete-pair persistence in the existing lease package: one fenced CAS writes both plan artifacts and their pair generation, versions and digests after validating both outputs, canonical meaningful change and the reserved rejection identity. Use this from direct-issue planner completion instead of separate UpdateArtifact calls. Pair completeness means the exact two recorded artifacts belong to that completed generation, even when only one body changed. Any ordinary single report write invalidates the completion marker while retaining tracked-generation status; admission uses only the R1 predicate. Extend existing authorized direct-issue staging to mark completion only after both staged versions are verified; preserve its existing plan-mode restrictions. Human approval and agent review admission reject IncompletePair as precisely defined in R1, not marker-less compatible initial pairs. Atomic pair failure leaves the prior complete pair intact; legacy interrupted separate writes remain blocked. Do not add a fork operation or allow agent imports to mint completion.

   Legacy pending agent state may be hydrated only while the authenticated review and its exact rejected pair remain present and bound. Missing provenance stops with the matrix's real recovery command. Authenticated human re-rejection with both reports present and a positive trusted limit can establish a new complete-draft attempt against the current pair, including mixed legacy inputs, but cannot approve that mixed pair; the next successful pair replacement must precede approval. Detect incomplete generations in RecordHumanReview APPROVED as well as VerifyApproval.

   For non-fork, non-PR direct issue state, RecordHumanReview CHANGES_REQUESTED always persists a human approval obligation, independent of invocation flags. Reserve a human draft attempt using fenced CAS and trusted PlanReplanLimit before any planner run, counted per authenticated rejection identity; failure, refusal, unchanged output and restart consume rather than refund it. A new authenticated human rejection with both reports present establishes an allowance bounded by the trusted limit; at zero it grants no draft. No automatic invocation loops through human review. Preserve the obligation across report changes, claims, checkpoints and agent review. Discharge only on authenticated exact-pair human approval; otherwise clear only for a changed WorkUnit or maintainer-authorized discard-checkpoint. Base/policy moves preserve the obligation even when carry removes both reports for an identical WorkUnit. Modify `internal/lease/carry.go:31` carryApprovalEvidence and its invalidation route at :102, inside existing coordinator approval/acquisition fencing: preserve the obligation and rejection identity/draft consumption independently of report/generation removal when the WorkUnit is unchanged. Removed reports cannot retain a usable completion marker; the next authorized planner must mint a new generation, subject to remaining draft allowance, and still stop for fresh human approval. Changed WorkUnit clears obsolete obligation and pair tracking with removed reports so the next planner is not blocked by stale T. Apply this digest-based clearing before both carry and the `manager.go:795` base-branch-change invalidation path: changed task clears obligation/T, identical task preserves obligation/rejection/consumption even on branch change. Retained authenticated findings remain deliverable to a permitted replacement planner after base/policy movement; stale bindings block approval/reuse, not feedback delivery (N5). Retained complete reports keep C; existing approval transitions and binding checks decide carry versus fresh approval. Do not broaden carry eligibility or change PR/fork behavior. Route all callers through this invariant before GateNone and agent review; node may stop but gains no continuation. Fork/PR protocols and behavior remain unchanged.

2. **Persistent validation allowance.** Add coordinator-owned ValidationRepairCount plus task/policy/base key to IssueState and a direct-coordinator fenced ReserveValidationRepair method in existing lease files. Load limit from approved base; reject gateway/fork/PR calls and mismatched nonempty keys. Initialize missing legacy fields inside the first reservation. Reserve before each automatic developer repair, even when resuming recorded failure at round zero; the R2 explicitly instructed initial round is requested work and retains the existing override without reservation or reset. Failed reservation runs no developer; admitted failing/canceled run spends an attempt. Reset only on changed approved task/policy/base revision, not new claims, plans, heads, staging, human review or checkpoint discard (`internal/lease/checkpoint_discard.go:96`). Explicit implement's admitted first requested round consumes/grants no automatic allowance; without developer instructions it still refuses all-pre-existing failures. Preserve shared PR/fork counters and semantics.

3. **Shared typed decisions and continuation (F4).** Modify `engine.go` WorkOptions, preflight/rolesForPhase/ExecuteWork, `execute_setup.go`, `execute_plan.go`, `execute_review.go`, `execute_implementation.go` and `execute_validation.go`. Add a side-effect-free typed transition classifier used by selection, preflight, setup and execution; authoritative bindings, budget and safety determine decisions, never error prose or next_action strings. Direct coordinator methods perform final fenced admission. Reconcile checkpoints before looping. Keep one claim/heartbeat and options object, reload authoritative state between transitions, and stop on refusal, invalid artifacts, no progress or terminal errors. Preflight the selected planner when rejection after reused-plan review can reach it; avoid speculative planner preflight when budget or interactive mode prevents it. Preserve existing shared bare-verdict fallback for opted-out paths.

   Modify `internal/cli/work.go` and `selection.go` to retain requested versus derived phase. Before claiming under --next, apply the R2 option-aware matrix and skip typed blocked decisions (bare feedback without effective planner guidance, human obligation with no eligible draft, incomplete legacy provenance, exhausted plan/human allowance or repair allowance without a requested developer override); continue to the next ready issue. An eligible human draft may be selected once within allowance. Revalidate after claim to handle races. Node selection applies the human-obligation invariant but otherwise retains existing accounting and scheduling.

   Set an explicit workRun tester-resume decision after verifying implementation evidence.
